sentences.text:
The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender
 M.A.C.M.A No.3606 of 2008
Judgment:

Aggrieved by the award dated 22.05.2008 in O.P.No.1005 of 2006 passed by the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Principal District Judge) at Nalgonda, the claimants have preferred this appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Principal District Judge) at Nalgonda
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard both sides and perused the entire material on record.
3.

The claim petition was filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.12,00,000/- and the Tribunal granted compensation of Rs.2,78,500/- with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit against respondent Nos.1 and 2 respectively.
4. The claimant Nos.1 and 2 are the parents of the deceased and the claimant No.3 is the sister of the deceased.
As per the case of the claimants, the deceased died in an accident on 17.10.2006 while going on a motorcycle to meet his friend.
The accident happened at 5.00pm.
The offending vehicle which is auto hit the motorcycle KS, J MACMA_3606_2008 resulting in the deceased falling down and while undergoing treatment, he died on the same day.
5. The manner in which the accident has taken place and the liability of the Insurance Company are not in dispute.

6. The learned Tribunal having found that the employer of the offer letter was not examined to prove that he is offered a salary of Rs.20,000/- to Rs.25,000/- per month, considered the income at Rs.36,000/- per annum and granted compensation.
Keeping in view that the deceased was an MBA student, this Court is inclined to take the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/-.
7. While computing the compensation, the future prospects were not considered by the Tribunal.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi 1 has held that while considering the compensation in cases of death, the future prospects of the self-employed shall also be considered.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Having regard to the age of deceased as 24 years as on the date of accident and occupation as self-employed, if 40 percent of the income is 2017 (6) 170 (SC) KS, J MACMA_3606_2008 included as future prospects, the monthly income would come to Rs.11200/-
(Rs.8,000+3,200).

As per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Smt. Sarla Varma v Delhi Transport Corporation 2, 50% of the income has to be deducted towards personal expenses as the deceased was a bachelor which comes to Rs.5,600/-.

entities.text: Smt. Sarla Varma v Delhi Transport Corporation 2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus the annual contribution of the deceased to the claimants would be of Rs.67,200/- (Rs.5,600X12).

As per Schedule II of the Act, if the said annual contribution arrived at is multiplied with relevant multiplier to the age of the claimant i.e.18,
the total amount comes to Rs.12,09,600/-.
Thus, the claimants are entitled for the said amount under the head of loss of dependency.

sentences.text: As regards the consortium to be paid, claimant Nos.1 and 2 are entitled to Rs.40,000/- each towards consortium as decided by the Hon'ble Apex court in case of Pranay Sethi (1 Supra).
With regard to the funeral expenses and loss of estate, the claimants are entitled for Rs.30,000/-.
Under the head of loss of love and affection and transportation, the Tribunal has granted an amount of Rs.12,000/- and this Court is not inclined to interfere with the said finding.

10. Therefore, the claimants are awarded the compensation as below:
 Head Compensation awarded  (1) Loss of dependency Rs.12,09,600  (2) Funeral expenses and Loss of Estate Rs.30,000  (3) Loss of filial consortium Rs.80,000(for 1st  and2nd claimants)
 (4) Loss of Love and affection Rs.12,000/-
 (to 3rd claimant)
 Total compensation awarded Rs.13,31,600/-
11.
In the result, the Motor Accident Miscellaneous Appeal is allowed enhancing the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal from Rs.2,78,500/- to Rs.13,31,600/-.
(a) The enhanced amount shall carry interest at 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization.
KS, J MACMA_3606_2008 (b) The claimants shall pay the court fee on the enhanced amount of compensation.
(c) The respondents shall deposit the amount within a period of (8) weeks from the date of receipt of copy of judgment.
On such deposit, claimants are entitled to withdraw the entire amount without furnishing the security.
(d) Amounts shall be apportioned in terms of the ratio decided by the Tribunal in the Award.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
No order as to costs.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The claim petition was filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.12,00,000/- and the Tribunal granted compensation of Rs.2,78,500/- with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit against respondent Nos.1 and 2 respectively.
As per the case of the claimants, the deceased died in an accident on 17.10.2006 while going on a motorcycle to meet his friend.
The accident happened at 5.00pm.
The offending vehicle which is auto hit the motorcycle KS, J MACMA_3606_2008 resulting in the deceased falling down and while undergoing treatment, he died on the same day.
6. The learned Tribunal having found that the employer of the offer letter was not examined to prove that he is offered a salary of Rs.20,000/- to Rs.25,000/- per month, considered the income at Rs.36,000/- per annum and granted compensation.
Having regard to the age of deceased as 24 years as on the date of accident and occupation as self-employed, if 40 percent of the income is 2017 (6) 170 (SC) KS, J MACMA_3606_2008 included as future prospects, the monthly income would come to Rs.11200/-
(Rs.8,000+3,200).
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The Hon'ble Apex Court in case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi 1 has held that while considering the compensation in cases of death, the future prospects of the self-employed shall also be considered.
As per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Smt. Sarla Varma v Delhi Transport Corporation 2, 50% of the income has to be deducted towards personal expenses as the deceased was a bachelor which comes to Rs.5,600/-.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Thus the annual contribution of the deceased to the claimants would be of Rs.67,200/- (Rs.5,600X12).
As per Schedule II of the Act, if the said annual contribution arrived at is multiplied with relevant multiplier to the age of the claimant i.e.18,
the total amount comes to Rs.12,09,600/-.
Thus, the claimants are entitled for the said amount under the head of loss of dependency.
As regards the consortium to be paid, claimant Nos.1 and 2 are entitled to Rs.40,000/- each towards consortium as decided by the Hon'ble Apex court in case of Pranay Sethi (1 Supra).
With regard to the funeral expenses and loss of estate, the claimants are entitled for Rs.30,000/-.
Under the head of loss of love and affection and transportation, the Tribunal has granted an amount of Rs.12,000/- and this Court is not inclined to interfere with the said finding.
10. Therefore, the claimants are awarded the compensation as below:
 Head Compensation awarded  (1) Loss of dependency Rs.12,09,600  (2) Funeral expenses and Loss of Estate Rs.30,000  (3) Loss of filial consortium Rs.80,000(for 1st  and2nd claimants)
 (4) Loss of Love and affection Rs.12,000/-
 (to 3rd claimant)
 Total compensation awarded Rs.13,31,600/-
11.
In the result, the Motor Accident Miscellaneous Appeal is allowed enhancing the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal from Rs.2,78,500/- to Rs.13,31,600/-.
(a) The enhanced amount shall carry interest at 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization.
KS, J MACMA_3606_2008 (b) The claimants shall pay the court fee on the enhanced amount of compensation.
(c) The respondents shall deposit the amount within a period of (8) weeks from the date of receipt of copy of judgment.
On such deposit, claimants are entitled to withdraw the entire amount without furnishing the security.
(d) Amounts shall be apportioned in terms of the ratio decided by the Tribunal in the Award.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
